initial_plan.can_answer_question: partly: crash data has no miles-driven exposure denominator, so it cannot measure deaths per mile; it can show annual recorded motorist-death counts
initial_plan.denominator: none; an annual count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC crash rows dated from 2013 through 2025 inclusive

data_check_interpretation.findings: The planned period contains 2,132,218 crash rows; every year from 2013 through 2025 has records spanning January 1 through December 31. There are no NULL crash dates in the file, and no missing number_of_motorist_killed values on the planned rows. The file extends from 2012-07-01 to 2026-06-11, so the later partial 2026 coverage is outside the plan.
data_check_interpretation.row_decisions: Keep all planned-year crash rows. No rows are excluded or counted differently due to missing dates or missing motorist-death counts; annual groupings are full calendar years. No miles-driven exposure rows exist in this dataset.

final_plan.can_answer_question: partly: cannot answer whether the risk per mile declined because the dataset contains no miles-driven exposure; it can describe annual recorded motorist-death counts
final_plan.metric: annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed, interpreted as the number of motorist deaths recorded in crash rows
final_plan.population: all police-reported NYC crash rows with crash_date in calendar years 2013–2025 inclusive
final_plan.limitations: The crash file has no miles driven, so annual death counts do not measure per-mile risk. The count includes motorist deaths recorded in reported crashes and does not account for changes in driving exposure. Data checks found 0 missing dates and 0 missing motorist-death counts among 2,132,218 planned-year rows; each planned year spans the full calendar year.
